name: Local complementation of graph states
aliases: local Clifford equivalence of graph states
summary: Applying X(π/2) to a vertex of a graph state and Z(−π/2) to its neighbours complements the neighbourhood of that vertex.
description:
A *graph state* is drawn as a phase-free Z-spider for every vertex of the graph, each with one output, connected by Hadamard edges according to the edges of the graph. *Local complementation* $G\star u$ of a graph about a vertex $u$ toggles every edge between two neighbours of $u$. Van den Nest showed that $G\star u$ is obtained from $G$ by local Clifford operations: an $X_{\pi/2}$ rotation on $u$ and a $Z_{-\pi/2}$ rotation on each neighbour of $u$ (up to a global phase; complex conjugating both sides gives the version with the opposite signs).

Duncan and Perdrix proved this equation in the ZX-calculus, and showed that it holds if and only if the Hadamard gate has an [Euler decomposition](../euler-decomposition-hadamard/) into $\pi/2$ rotations; this was the original reason to add the Euler decomposition as an axiom. Fusing the phases into the spiders, this equation is the basis of the graph-like [local complementation simplification](../local-complementation/) and of [pivoting](../graph-state-pivot/).
parameter_notes: n is the number of neighbours of u (shown for n = 3). The neighbours may be connected to further vertices of the graph state, which are left unchanged; existing edges between neighbours are toggled. The scalar is for neighbours that are not yet connected; since every Hadamard edge carries a factor 1/√2, in general it is √2 to the power (number of edges added − number of edges removed).

source.location: Section 5 (Local Complementation), theorem of Van den Nest
